script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for May 11. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
You spend about 26 years of your life asleep.  That seems like wasted time—but sleep isn't nothing.  It's when your brain consolidates memories, flushes toxins, and repairs damage.

While you sleep, your brain replays the day's experiences, moving important information from short-term to long-term memory. Students who sleep after studying remember more than those who stay awake. Sleep is learning's partner. Your brain produces toxic waste products during the day.  During sleep, the glymphatic system—a cleanup crew—flushes these toxins away.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Rest is productive.  Sleep teaches that doing nothing is sometimes doing everything—the work just happens invisibly.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Sleep Audit - Evaluate Your Rest.

Here's your activity: Track your sleep for a week—hours, quality, how you feel. Are you getting enough? Sleep deprivation accumulates silently. Notice the connection between sleep and your thinking, mood, and energy. Adjust accordingly. This helps you assess and improve sleep habits.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about what happens when you sleep can be applied to sleep audit - evaluate your rest. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
